report:
Reviewed the complete compiler_conditions claim, four ordinary implementation associations (annotations.rs, mod.rs, observe.rs, rustc.rs), and six associated tests; there are no TODO/N/A entries. Requirements: both compilers execute for valid fixtures, unqualified ERROR/WARN apply independently to both, qualified conditions restrict applicability, matching is exhaustive and one-to-one per compiler, a shared marker does not permit two diagnostics on either compiler, only Sage contributes snapshots, and compiler-condition changes need a semantic explanation.
Implementation: annotations::parse accepts precisely ERROR/WARN with no condition, if SAGE, or if rustc; Marker::applies_to implements the selection. CompileTest::prepare invokes rustc::check before SageHost/observe::collect and retains both results until both checks finish, including combining failures. rustc::check returns only Result<(), String>; successful Output is exclusively observe::collect's Sage observations, diagnostics, and inspection-log queries. match_compiler_diagnostics filters independently by compiler and severity, builds eligible location edges, and requires an augmenting one-to-one matching with no unassigned diagnostics. Thus excess markers and excess diagnostics fail independently. The semantic-explanation obligation is an authoring/review policy documented in the captured contribution guidance; the new synthetic matrix expresses contract scenarios rather than blessing real compiler differences.
Tests: only_real_line_comment_directives_are_interpreted rejects malformed/unknown conditions and excludes string/block-comment pseudo-markers. compiler_qualifiers_and_shared_counts_are_independent parses all six combinations of severity and qualification, checks both compilers against zero and one diagnostic, and rejects two diagnostics for each combination; it directly covers SAGE filtering and shared per-compiler counts. evaluated_source_retains_blank_lines_indentation_and_unicode runs a real shared ERROR fixture through prepare and asserts Sage diagnostic text, proving one marker accepts one actual diagnostic from each compiler. rustc_is_mandatory_and_warnings_can_be_enabled_in_source checks clean execution, missing rustc warning failure, qualified warning success with empty Sage diagnostics, and qualified rustc error success. shared_markers_must_match_both_compilers rejects a rustc-only warning under an unqualified marker and a missing rustc-specific error. explicit_edition_and_rustc_warning_marker invokes the public macro with a rustc-only warning and an empty diagnostic snapshot. Snapshot separation also follows structurally from rustc's unit return and Sage-only Output construction; it does not depend on discarded rustc text formatting.
Source inspection is distinct from execution. cargo test -p sage-test-harness compile::rustc_tests --lib passed both tests. cargo test -p sage-test-harness compiler_conditions_review_tests --lib passed the new matrix test (1/1). Early builds encountered an unrelated concurrent token-rendering compile failure, followed by a fixed test-only Severity ownership error; neither was a behavioral reproduction. Workspace build and mandatory delegated post-codegen/sanity checks are coordinated by the parent. No production behavior defect was found.
